doc.title: Exception Handling
doc.para: Exception Handling An exception is a so-called "exception" that is unexpected in normal processing, and in most cases, you can think of it as being the same as an "error".

Where Exceptions Occur An exception can occur anywhere in a program. Causing an exception to occur is also called "throwing an exception (throw)". For example, suppose the following script causes an error.
"3%0"!; // "Attempted division by 0" An exception occurs
There are cases like this where an exception obviously occurs, but there are also cases where it is not known whether one will occur or not.

Catching Exceptions Using the try (try) keyword and the catch (catch) keyword, you can catch exceptions. For example, to catch an exception that might occur in the example above, you can write a script like this:
try // Because an exception might occur { func1(); // An exception might occur here } catch // Catch the exception { // When an exception occurs, this section is executed inform("Failed to load image."); // Display a message }
In this way, if you write processing that might cause an exception inside a try block, you can execute the catch block when an exception occurs. Error handling can be written cleanly like this.
If no exception occurs in the try block, the catch block is not executed either.
You can write anything in a try block. As in this example, there may be cases where an exception obviously could occur on that line, but even when an exception occurs deep inside function calls within function calls, if you write try ... catch, you can return here as soon as the exception occurs.
If an exception occurs, the remaining processing in the block is suspended, and execution returns to where the try is located.
If an exception occurs again inside the catch block, the exception will not be caught at this location. As it is, the exception goes back up through function calls, etc., and if an exception is caught with try somewhere else, it will be caught there.
Another exception might occur between the time an exception is thrown and the time it reaches the catch block, but the behavior is undefined.
If an exception is not caught anywhere in the script, the exception leaves the script as it is, is passed to the application, and is handled there.
Normally, such an exception will halt execution as an error, so it is recommended to write try ... catch in places where errors are likely to occur whenever possible.
